newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia bank NKBM sees 96 net profit up 16.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia bank NKBM sees 96 net profit up 16.7 pct.

text.p: Slovenia's third largest bank Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor (NKBM) said on Wednesday its 1996 net profit was expected to rise to 2.1 billion tolars ($14.8 million) from 1.8 billion in 1995.

"The profit is up due to expanded business in all banking areas, including tolar and foreign exchange activities of individuals and companies," Darko Tolar, a member of the NKBM management board told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Balance sheet assets rose to 200 billion tolars according to unrevised figures from 168.43 billion at the end of 1995.
The bank, which has never paid any dividends, said this year would be no different, as it was fully state-owned and would pour back all profits into reserves.

In an move to expand its business further NKBM on January 1 took over a third of listed Hipotekarna Banka Brezice (HBB), buying 1.35 billion tolars of HBB's assets and an adequate share of its liabilities.
"This Monday we opened two new offices in Brezice and Krsko that we took over from HBB," Tolar said.
